premise: Automate what can be automated and put a gate in front of what cannot. Every check below states which side of that line it sits on.

checks.requirement: State "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases." clearly and prominently on the site.
checks.quote_basis: Section 5 ("Identifying Yourself as an Associate") names the sentence. The material-breach consequence sits in Section 6 (Term and Termination), not Section 5: "any violation of Section 5 and as specified in the Program Policies will be deemed a material breach of this Agreement." Both read on the live page 2026-11-20; the row previously attributed both halves to Section 5.
checks.evidence: The exact sentence appears in a strip directly under the masthead on every generated page, and again in the footer. tools/check_site.py fails the build if any page is missing it.
checks.gate: none

checks.requirement: Put the disclosure where it is hard to miss, next to the endorsement, not only on an about page or at the end.
checks.quote_basis: "Place it so it's hard to miss... Disclosures are likely to be missed if they appear only on an ABOUT ME or profile page, at the end of posts or videos, or anywhere that requires a person to click MORE."
checks.evidence: Above-the-fold strip under the masthead on all pages, plus a disclosure line immediately above each outbound product button. The footer repeat is supplementary, not the primary disclosure.
checks.gate: none

checks.requirement: Mark every paid or sponsored outbound link with rel="sponsored".
checks.quote_basis: "Mark links that are advertisements or paid placements (commonly called paid links) with the sponsored value."
checks.evidence: Every anchor to an Amazon domain is emitted with rel="sponsored noopener". tools/check_site.py walks all generated HTML and fails if any Amazon link lacks it.
checks.gate: none

checks.requirement: Do not obscure that a link goes to an Amazon Site.
checks.quote_basis: Section 6(w) of the Participation Requirements (Content on your Site) prohibits a link shortening service, button, hyperlink or other ad placement used in a manner that makes it unclear you are linking to an Amazon Site. Read and quoted 2026-11-20; the earlier citation to 2(b) was wrong, because Section 2 ("Links on Your Site") has only subsections (a) and (b).
checks.evidence: The site publishes direct amazon.com/dp/<ASIN> destinations wherever a link is written out. Three buy buttons use a supplied link.amazon short code; each names the product in its text and each card carries the full official listing URL as its source line. Whether the supplied short links are acceptable in the enrolled account is FLG-006 / FLG-026 and is unchanged by this clause check.
checks.gate: Owner action: run the FLG-006 test (one Special Link per product, destination and Associates report confirmed) before scaling. Any change of CTA destination is a decision in SG-13, not an automated edit.

checks.requirement: Show price and availability only if Amazon serves that data, or it is obtained through the Product Advertising / Creators API.
checks.quote_basis: Section 2(b) permits displaying price and availability only in those two cases. The same subsection adds that a price shown in a comparison format alongside non-Amazon prices must show the lowest "new" price and, where Amazon provides it, the lowest "used" Amazon price - read on the live page 2026-11-20, and a condition on any future decision to display prices.
checks.evidence: The site stores no price and renders none — no price, no discount, no promotional code, no delivery estimate, anywhere. Prices are visible only on the Amazon page after a click. A checker rule fails the build if a currency pattern appears in generated HTML.
checks.gate: none

checks.requirement: Do not make inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or misleading claims about a product.
checks.quote_basis: Section 2(b) prohibition on inaccurate or misleading product claims, with the 64 GB / 128 GB example.
checks.evidence: Every published specification is copied from the listing and tagged with a source id and a capture date. Where the listing contradicts itself (P1 capacity units, P2 preset count) both readings are shown and the conflict is named rather than resolved silently.
checks.gate: Human review of editorial prose before each new guide is published. The automated check can prove a claim is cited; it cannot prove the citation supports the claim.

checks.requirement: Do not claim first-hand experience with a product that has not been handled.
checks.quote_basis: "You can't talk about your experience with a product you haven't tried."
checks.evidence: The voice rules ban first-person use claims, durability claims, and first-person testing phrasing. Every product page says plainly that no unit has been handled and that the numbers come from the listing.
checks.gate: Editorial review. See suggestion SG-06: buying one unit per category would let the site make experience claims honestly.

checks.requirement: Affiliate pages must carry original value rather than restating the merchant's listing, or they fall under the thin-affiliation and scaled-content-abuse policies.
checks.quote_basis: Both policies are named explicitly in Google's spam policies.
checks.evidence: Each guide answers a question the listing cannot: how to compare basket against oven form, which specification decides the fit, and how to set up a thermometer against the USDA minimums. The build check enforces a minimum word count and an internal-link requirement on every article.
checks.gate: A human must judge whether the writing is actually useful. Word count is a floor, not a defence.

checks.requirement: Keep the intended ASIN and the observed redirect in separate fields; never merge them.
checks.quote_basis: Section 2(a) requires Special Links to carry the assigned Associates ID; the ASIN is the checkable product identifier.
checks.evidence: Field separation is structural. data/products.json keeps intended_asin, intended_listing_url, confirmation_date and intent_source as flat null fields, and keeps observed_redirect_target, observed_asin and live_recheck_2026_11_20 in separate fields. data/verification.json keeps an intended object and an observed object per product. On 2026-11-20 the earlier 2026-11-19 verification records were found to copy observed ASINs into intended.asin and cite S16 (a NIST page) as the source; those values were blanked and the correction is recorded in that file. No intended ASIN is confirmed by the owner, so no intended value is shown as verified (FLG-001).
checks.gate: Automated: tools/verify_site.py fails if any intended ASIN is filled without an owner-confirmation record, or if an intended source is S16 or any other non-owner reference. Owner action: confirm each link's intended ASIN in the Associates workflow (FLG-001).

checks.requirement: Confirm the tracking ID shopnow047c-20 is present on the Special Links actually published.
checks.quote_basis: Section 2(a): Special Links must use the Associates ID assigned to the account.
checks.evidence: The resolved URLs served to this session carried query parameters but no visible tag= value, so the ID could not be confirmed from outside the account. Nothing about the supplied links is called invalid; the check simply cannot be completed without the Associates dashboard.
checks.gate: Owner action: open SiteStripe or the Associates dashboard and confirm tag=shopnow047c-20 on each of the five links. Tracked as Q-02.

checks.requirement: Links into a product list (search, deal event, department page) require additional original content on the site.
checks.quote_basis: Section 2(b): when linking to pages with product lists you must have additional original content relevant to the Special Link.
checks.evidence: The only category link on the site points at the Air Fryers storefront (internal site check, not an external source) and appears inside the comparison guide, which carries its own analysis. No bare list links are published.
checks.gate: Review any future category link before it ships.

checks.requirement: Keep outbound commerce links from crowding out the answer the reader came for.
checks.quote_basis: The people-first content guidance and the page-experience guidance both penalise interruption over substance.
checks.evidence: Each guide opens with the answer, then the reasoning, and only then the product cards. Product cards are capped at two per article by the build.
checks.gate: none

checks.requirement: Record only privacy-preserving events and never associate a tracking sub-tag with an individual user.
checks.quote_basis: Section 2(b): no sub-tag, other ID or reporting may be associated with a specific end user, including dynamically assigning sub-tags to arriving users.
checks.evidence: The outbound counter runs entirely in the visitor's browser, stores a single aggregate count per product in localStorage, and sends nothing. No per-user identifier is created, so no sub-tag could be tied to one. See content/measurement.md.
checks.gate: If a self-hosted endpoint is ever enabled, it must not set cookies and must not store IP addresses — see Q-13.

checks.requirement: Do not assert popularity, trending status or superiority without a dated source.
checks.quote_basis: Self-assessment question: does the content provide insight beyond the obvious, and is the heading free of exaggeration.
checks.evidence: Where the listing itself displays a badge such as Amazon's Choice or a sales figure, it is quoted with the capture date and attributed to the listing. No editorial page claims a product is best-selling, trending or better.
checks.gate: Editorial review of any new superlative.

checks.requirement: Do not display Amazon customer reviews or star ratings, in part or in whole, unless a link to them was obtained through Creators API or PA API (Participation Requirements section 6(t)).
checks.quote_basis: Section 6(t), verbatim from the live page 2026-11-20: no customer review or star rating may be displayed or used "in part or in whole" unless a link to it was obtained through Creators API or PA API, under the License terms. The permission is a link to the review, not a rating value to print.
checks.evidence: No star rating, rating count or review text appears anywhere on the site; tools/check_site.py rule D10 fails the build on a rendered rating pattern. The 2026-11-19 decision to remove ratings now rests on a located clause rather than a remembered one.
checks.gate: D10-no-ratings (tools/check_site.py).

checks.requirement: No price tracking and no price alerting functionality on the site, unless otherwise agreed by Amazon (Participation Requirements section 6(y)).
checks.quote_basis: Section 6(y), verbatim: "Unless otherwise agreed by Amazon, your Site must not have price tracking and/or price alerting functionality." Read on the live page 2026-11-20.
checks.evidence: The site stores no price and offers no watch, alert, notify-me, back-in-stock or drop-tracking feature, so it complies by absence. The row exists to keep it that way: price alerts are the most commonly proposed return-visitor feature in affiliate plans, and this one is not buildable here without an agreement with Amazon.
checks.gate: Refused on this row at proposal time, not deferred. Recorded on ideas.html as an idea the site will not do.

checks.requirement: Do not artificially generate clicks or impressions on the site, or create Sessions on an Amazon Site, by way of a robot or software program or otherwise (Participation Requirements section 6(s)).
checks.quote_basis: Section 6(s), verbatim: "You will not artificially generate clicks or impressions on your Site or create Sessions on an Amazon Site, whether by way of a robot or software program or otherwise." Read 2026-11-20. Section 5 of the Commission Income Statement adds that tags "should only be used to benefit from Amazon Associates commissions", and that claiming the same traffic through another program by manipulating or combining attribution links may end in withheld commissions.
checks.evidence: Nothing on the site clicks its own links. The only outbound automation is a passive listener that counts a real visitor's click in that visitor's browser (assets/app.js); it opens no window, prefetches no Amazon URL and sends nothing to any server. The link checker resolves internal targets only; the intake tool records where a supplied link lands as a dated source observation, not as a click event. Any future automated promotion must respect this row: no self-clicking crawler, no synthetic traffic, no prefetch of Special Links.
checks.gate: If any automation capable of reaching a URL is added, gate it: outbound requests from CI must be limited to listing reads and must never carry a tag parameter.

checks.requirement: Offer no consideration, reward or incentive for using Special Links; keep Special Links out of Amazon's customer-generated content; send email and direct messages only to people who opted in (sections 6(g) and 6(p), and section 4).
checks.quote_basis: Section 6(g) bars offering "any consideration, reward, or incentive (including any money, rebate, discount, points, donation to charity or other organization, or other benefit) for using Special Links". Section 6(p) bars Special Links in content placed on an Amazon Site, naming a customer review, forum, Wish List or guide. Section 4 permits Special Links in emails, SMS and direct messaging from your social media Sites only where "such communications are solicited (i.e., opted into by the receiving customer)".
checks.evidence: No giveaway, rebate, cashback, discount or points offer is tied to a link anywhere; nothing is posted to Amazon; the site sends no email and ships no signup form. The row constrains future plans as much as present state: a lead magnet attached to a newsletter carrying Special Links needs a real opt-in record, and a share-to-unlock mechanic must not become an incentive to click.
checks.gate: Review at proposal time. Reader capture stays open because no provider is connected; when one is, the opt-in record is what makes section 4 hold.

checks.requirement: Do not add to, delete from or otherwise alter Program Content; do not frame an Amazon Site; do not use Program Content to imply endorsement (sections 6(a), 6(n) and 6(d)).
checks.quote_basis: Section 6(a): Program Content may not be added to, deleted from or otherwise altered "in any way, including by adding additional information", except proportional resizing of an image or truncation that does not materially alter meaning. Section 6(n) forbids framing an Amazon Site or any part of it within your Site, including in an embedded web view, while noting that displaying a Special Link per section 2 is not a violation. Section 6(d) forbids using Program Content, including a name or likeness in it, so as to imply endorsement, sponsorship or a commercial tie-in.
checks.evidence: No Amazon page is embedded or framed and no Amazon image, banner or API block is displayed: the product cards are typographic label art made for this site, and listing text is quoted with attribution rather than rendered as Program Content. Whether editorial judgement printed beside a quoted spec field counts as "adding additional information" to Program Content is a reading the owner should confirm rather than assume, which is why this row is partial and not met.
checks.gate: Keep the standing rule that Program Content is never rendered as a widget. Any API-supplied image or block is checked against 6(a) before it ships, not after.

checks.requirement: The Site must contain original content, be publicly available, and be identified in the Associates application; third-party material must carry significant commentary, analysis or transformation (Participation Requirements section 1).
checks.quote_basis: Section 1: "Your Site(s) must contain original content and be publicly available via the website address provided in the application. Original content utilizing third-party materials must contain significant commentary, analysis, or transformation to any materials you include." The same section requires the Site to be identified in the application and lists unsuitable sites, including those carrying false, deceptive, libelous or defamatory materials.
checks.evidence: The original value today is the dated register: every figure traced to a named listing snapshot, both readings published where a listing contradicts itself, and comparison built from spec fields rather than adjectives. The site is publicly available at the Pages URL. Unresolved: whether this address is registered in the account, and whether volume publishing of generated guides would still satisfy the significant-commentary test. That is the eligibility floor under the automation brief, and it is why each planned guide is gated on a human-verified source row rather than on word count.
checks.gate: One row per guide in the editorial plan: the named official source, the dated capture, and what the site added that the listing does not contain. A guide that cannot fill those three is not published.

clause_verification: Clause numbers and quoted wording were re-read from the live Program Policies page (page states Updated 2026-04-14) and the Operating Agreement (2025-10-15) on 2026-11-20. Corrections: the customer-ratings rule is Section 6 item (t); URL obscuring is 6(v); the shortener rule is 6(w). Earlier drafts attached those three rules to Section 2, which on that page is titled "Links on Your Site" and has subsections (a) and (b) only. Every clause cited here is recorded with its quotation in data/policy-clause-map.json, and gate D35 fails the release if a clause letter that is not in that map is cited.

citation_correction_2026_11_20.what: Three clauses were cited to a Section 2 letter that does not exist, and two of them were then recorded on this site as impossible to find. A second pass, reading the page section by section instead of searching for a remembered number, located all of them.
citation_correction_2026_11_20.detail: Section 2 ("Links on Your Site") has subsections (a) and (b) only. The reviews/ratings, URL-obscuring and link-shortener clauses are sections 6(t), 6(v) and 6(w); price alerts are 6(y); synthetic traffic is 6(s); incentives are 6(g). The price, comparison-format, misleading-claims, sub-tag, product-list and tag-as-parameter rules really are 2(b) and were cited correctly.
citation_correction_2026_11_20.method: Every clause is transcribed from the page served on 2026-11-20 at https://affiliate-program.amazon.com/help/operating/policies (header: Updated April 14, 2026) and recorded clause by clause in data/policy-clause-map.json; gate D35 refuses a citation whose letter is not in that map.
citation_correction_2026_11_20.not_claimed: Nothing here asserts that this account is enrolled, that the tracking ID is valid, or that the supplied short links comply. Those stay owner-only.
